title: Route a back-in-time-blocked VCF estate through a greenfield stretched domain
prompt:
Build a PowerShell module that produces the deployable architecture for the mixed VMware Cloud Foundation estate in `fixtures/estate.json`. The estate has two data sites, a stretched management domain, a shared legacy witness, and component builds that may make the apparent in-place VCF 9.1 upgrade order invalid.

Before implementing, use genuine network access to research the currently published Broadcom compatibility/interoperability and upgrade-path material relevant to every version in the fixture, including the VCF 9.1 back-in-time restriction and vSAN stretched-cluster witness placement and lifecycle. Record the sources you actually consulted in `artifacts/research-sources.json` as an object with a `consultedAt` ISO-8601 timestamp including a timezone and a non-empty `sources` array; each source entry must contain `publisher`, `title`, `url`, and a non-empty `usedFor` array. Choose the live Broadcom HTTPS sources yourself. The pinned normalized rules in `compatibility/vcf-9.1-snapshot.json`, not mutable live pages, are the implementation input for deterministic output.

Implement `VcfMixedEstateArchitecture/VcfMixedEstateArchitecture.psd1` and `.psm1`, exporting `New-VcfMixedEstateArchitecture`. The command must accept `-EstatePath`, `-CompatibilityPath`, and `-OutputPath`, read those JSON inputs, and write UTF-8 JSON to the output path. The installed `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer` PowerCLI module is a prerequisite: declare it in the manifest and use its initializer cmdlets to construct the greenfield specification, including `Initialize-VcfInstallerSddcSpec`, `Initialize-VcfInstallerSddcHostSpec`, `Initialize-VcfInstallerSddcVcenterSpec`, `Initialize-VcfInstallerSddcNetworkSpec`, and `Initialize-VcfInstallerDnsSpec`. Do not vendor VMware modules or replace their behavior, and do not contact or mutate an appliance.

Commit the command's output for the supplied inputs as `artifacts/architecture.json`. Its `greenfield.sddcSpec` must be a VCF 9.1.0.0 SddcSpec that validates against the `SddcSpec` schema in `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, copied from tag `9.1.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`. Its `greenfield.topology` must map every target management host to one of the two data sites and place a dedicated target witness in the independent witness site, outside either data fault domain and outside the data cluster. The old shared witness must remain with the retained legacy cluster.

The `migrationPlan` must validate against `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. It must use an ordered parallel-greenfield route around every pinned forbidden in-place transition, name every component from the estate exactly once with its current version, target version, disposition, and technical gate IDs, include the new dedicated witness, and order target deployment and witness placement before management-domain cutover. Derive targets and gates from the pinned snapshot. Do not add approval stages, policy checks, or operational workflow unrelated to those compatibility and topology constraints.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py` from the repository root. The verifier remains offline: it validates the research record and Broadcom URLs structurally but does not contact those URLs or prove that they were consulted.
